items.response: I don't know yet and don't want to guess; it depends on whether the CLI has an update check built in. The CLI is the restricted @acme/cli package on npm, so a notifier would be in its source if present. Action: search packages/cli for an update check (update-notifier or similar), find the interval and how to disable it, then answer the #eng question.

Quick reminder that the tsx change is still half done: package.json was edited by hand and the lockfile is not updated. Action: tell me which install command to use, or I'll run the usual install from the repo root, so the lockfile can be committed with it.

Will remove any leftover husky references. For the db: Postgres 16 is now the primary database (MySQL is retired) and migrations restart from the 0031_pg_baseline, so after your pull the local setup probably has an old MySQL-style DATABASE_URL or container. Local env goes in .env.local, not .env. Action: grep for .husky references and remove them, check DATABASE_URL (should be postgres://...@host:5432/acme) and the db container image, then bring up db and redis from docker-compose and run migrations, without deleting any volume unless you say so.

I'm not sure, and you said it changed in the migration, so I'd rather look than guess. Action: look in infra/ for the current tooling and any existing queue definitions, then tell you where an exports queue should go and what it's written in.

If those configs came back, Lena's PR is working against the cleanup, but I need to check what replaced them before saying so. For CORS, I'll allow only origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS (comma separated) and stop reflecting arbitrary origins. Action: look at the PR diff and the repo's current lint/format setup to flag the files, then change api CORS to parse CORS_ORIGINS, trim entries, allow exact matches only, and deny everything if it is unset, with tests.

I'll add retry with backoff to the CLI api client for 502, 503 and 504, with 3 tries total. I'd limit it to those statuses and keep GETs safe to retry; for non-idempotent requests I'll ask before retrying. Action: find the cli api client, add exponential backoff with a small jitter, test with mocked 502/503/504 then success and the exhausted case, and run the CLI tests.

I'll add a byte formatter in apps/web/lib with a test. I'll use 1024-based units labelled KB/MB/GB with one decimal (1.2 MB) and plain bytes below 1 KB; say so if you want 1000-based. Action: check naming conventions in apps/web/lib, add the util, and write tests for 0, under 1 KB, exact boundaries and large values, then run the web tests.

structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays and circular references; the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps and Sets into empty objects, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. structuredClone does throw on functions and loses class prototypes (you get plain objects). Action: none.
